reports.text:
HEDERSONVILLE, Tenn. – Weigh-in at any cut day of a championship event is a pretty nerve-wracking time, but when a $3.25 million total purse and championship check for $1.25 is on the line, it’s even more intense. The 62-angler roster for The Champions by World Bass Enterprises left it all out on Old Hickory Lake on Friday, fighting for a shot in Saturday’s final.
Saturday will bring the Top 15 back to Old Hickory for a one-day shootout for the biggest payday in bass-fishing history.

reports.title: Auburn’s Travis looking to cap strong season at Toyota Series Championship
reports.text:
Benjamin Travis ‘ final day at the Toyota Series event on Lake Guntersville in February had all the ingredients of a storybook first win. The Auburn University standout had always heard tournament anglers say, “when it’s your time, you can’t stop it.” So, when he told himself, “If I catch a 7-pounder, I think it’ll be enough to win,” then landed a largemouth over 7 two casts later to push his Day 3 limit over 25 pounds, he couldn’t help but believe it was his time to notch his first multi-day tournament victory.
He was so convinced that when the final angler to weigh in – Day 2 leader Kane Weekley – edged him by 1 ounce, it took Travis a moment to process what happened.

reports.text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. – You probably don’t think of Nashville as a fishing town, do you? No sir/ma’am, Nashville is most likely where you to go listen to country music, dance in a honky-tonk and have a good time with your friends. You don’t go there to catch a bass … right?

reports.text:
HENDERSONVILLE, Tenn. – As the hours tick down to the start of The Champions by World Bass Enterprises, the focus will quickly turn from “Who made it?” and “How much money are they going to win?” to “How will they catch ’em?”
The answers lie somewhere in the sprawling waters of Old Hickory Lake and the Cumberland River near Nashville.
Old Hickory is a historic lake by any measure. Named after President Andrew Jackson, it produced the world record walleye in 1960, and served as home for Johnny and June Carter Cash for 35 years. And as of Oct. 29-31, it’ll be the site of the richest bass tournament in history.

reports.title: Why The One That Got Away Can Be So Memorable
reports.text:
Anglers Journal founding editor Bill Sisson mentions the term ‘nursing home fish’ in his book “ Seasons of the Striper: Pursuing the Great American Gamefish .” It refers to fish caught long ago, the memories of which keep you company even when you’re too old to wet a line. These are the fish you can still see when you close your eyes, still feel their heft when you dream.
But I think that the ones that got away are just as important. Ask any angler about their most memorable fishing trip and sooner or later, you’ll hear about a fish that they couldn’t land.

reports.title: CN How To Nov 2026 How To: Crappie Dan explains how shadows, current, and underwater structure influence crappie behavior.
reports.text:
How To: Crappie Dan explains how shadows, current, and underwater structure influence crappie behavior.
In this episode of The Playbook, Crappie Dan explains how shadows, current, and underwater structure influence crappie and bass behavior. Fish often face into the current, positioning themselves where baitfish will naturally approach. During sunny conditions, they tend to hold in the shade created by stumps, brush, overhanging trees, and shoreline drop-offs, often near the edge of the light.
The key to success is proper boat positioning and bait placement. When casting or jigging, position your bait up current so it moves naturally toward the fish. Approaching from behind can spook them…

reports.title: Bank-Fishing Teen Nearly Breaks 21-Year-Old State Largemouth Bass Record
reports.text:
Some time around mid-morning on Oct. 3, 14-year-old Luke Mulholland of Zumbrota, Minnesota, took a break from his usual trout fishing. He decided to try for bass at Cascade Lake, located near Rochester.
He was casting a half-foot long Bucca Baits Trick Shad swim bait when he saw a disturbance on the lake surface.
“I was fishing and I saw a wake in the water, and I cast at it and I thought I snagged a log, it was just heavy,” said Luke, who’s been fishing since age 3.

But when the log started moving and hard fought his tackle, he knew it wasn’t a snag. It was so heavy, he then thought he hooked a turtle.

reports.title: Hit Lake Murray’s brush for fall crappie
reports.text:
Don’t miss the fall crappie bite
A s Lake Murray’s water temperature cools down in October, Capt. Brad Taylor of Taylor Outdoors said the crappie fishing gets cranked up.
“October is a great month because you can catch crappie in a number of ways, really just about any way you want to catch them will work,” he said.
One way Taylor targets them this time of year is by fishing brush in the main river channel.

Matching your jig to the size and shape of the main crappie forage can greatly increase your number of hookups.
Crappie Basics: Match the Hatch for More Crappie
By Keith Sutton
One of the simplest ways to improve your crappie fishing is to give the fish what they’re already looking for. That means matching your jig to the size and general shape of the forage crappie are feeding on.
If 2-inch minnows make up a big part of the crappie diet in the lake you’re fishing, for example, a 2-inch jig is a logical choice. If the fish are eating tiny shiners, you’ll probably do better with a smaller offering. The same principle applies when shad, fathead minnows or other forage dominate the menu.

reports.title: Yeopim Creek Fliers with Carolina ALL OUT
reports.text:
Fliers are among the most unique panfish in the Carolinas
T he Carolinas are full of numerous species of panfish, and for their size, they all fight like champs. They’re also very tasty. Fliers, although they are found throughout the southeast, are among the least widely distributed panfish, mostly living in swampy, acidic blackwater creeks with low pH.
Where you’ll find fliers, you can always count on finding other panfish as well. They overlap with crappie, bluegill, redbreast and shellcrackers, among other species.
